title: OKRs & Goals
description: Leadership teams: set quarterly objectives and key results, then check in weekly.

spec.useCase: Hollis Beaumont-Park leads a member-owned credit cooperative and uses this to see which objectives are on track and which key results are slipping.

business.name: Copperfield Cooperative
business.describes: A member-owned credit cooperative serving a mid-sized city.

tables.name: Objectives
tables.describes: The few outcomes the cooperative is aiming for this cycle and the next.
tables.subject: thing

values.objective_name: Members feel looked after from the first day
values.why: New members who are helped in week one stay for years and bring family.
Slow, fiddly applications are the top reason people go elsewhere.

values.objective_name: A website and app that members trust
values.why: Trust in the website is trust in us; one outage costs months of goodwill.

values.objective_name: Grow through members telling their friends
values.why: Most of our best members came by word of mouth, so we invest there first.

values.objective_name: Get the systems ready for double the members
values.why: Doubling the membership will strain the current tools unless we prepare early.

question.ask: How many objectives are at risk?
question.whyItMatters: Hollis opens the Monday leadership meeting with this.

text.text: Set a few objectives each cycle, measure each with two or three key results, and update the numbers every week. Progress adds up by itself.
This cycle
Key results
Progress is read straight from each key result: (current - start) / (target - start). Update the current value every week and everything above follows.
Objectives at risk or off track
Results that went down
Stale numbers
Ten minutes on Monday. Each owner updates their numbers before the meeting, not during it.
Update the current value of each key result you own
Set the trend: up, flat or down
If an objective is at risk, write what would change it
Pick one result the whole team should help with this week
Notes
An objective
Says what better looks like, in plain words.
Is something a team can influence this cycle.
Does not contain a number.
A key result
Has a start value, a target and a real way to measure it.
Describes an outcome, not an activity.
Is ambitious: reaching about seven tenths is a good cycle.

cells.text: Raise monthly referral signups from 12 to 60
Cut median days to a decision from 6 to 2
Raise welcome calls completed from 40% to 95%

text.text: How many per team
Two or three objectives, each with two or three key results. More than that and nothing gets finished.
What to do with a result that is already met
Raise the target or replace it. A result that is already green teaches nothing.
Run this at the end of every cycle with the whole leadership group.
Score
Read the average progress for each objective on the dashboard. Do not argue about decimals.
Questions
What did we learn about how we set targets?
Which result surprised us, up or down?
Which objective do we carry into the next cycle, and why?
What do we stop doing?
